texts.facts: In the present case, Detailed Accident Report (DAR) was filed on 12.09.2022 regarding a Road Traffic Accident, which took place on 22.05.2022 at 06:00 PM at Outer Ring Road, Wazirabad Flyover, 'Y' Point, Timar Pur, Delhi. It emerged from the DAR that on 22.05.2022, Smt. Phoolwati along with her son-in-law Sh. Bhim Sain was going to her house from a family function and when they reached the Wazirabad Flyover, suddenly they ran out of petrol. Sh. Bhim Sain parked their vehicle on a side safely when suddenly a vehicle i.e. chhota haathi bearing registration no. DL-1L-AF-2991 driven by respondent no. 1 in a very rash and negligent manner hit the vehicle of the petitioner from the back. 2. The vehicle bearing registration No. DL-1L-AF-2991 was being driven by respondent no.1 Mr. Aslam, owned by respondent no.2, Mr. Alauddin and insured with respondent no.3, TATA AIG Insurance Co. 3. It is the case of the petitioner that she was taken to Lok Nayak Hospital where her MLC bearing no. 1149/2022 was prepared. She has deposed to have been treated by Employees State Insurance Corporation as well as Usha Dental Clinic for dental treatment as also at Metro Hospital. MACT No. 745/2022 Phoolwati Vs. Aslam & ors. Page 2 of 29 4. During investigation, the IO arrested the driver of the said vehicle who is the respondent no. 1, Mr. Aslam. Later, he was released on bail. Case property was seized and mechanical inspection was got conducted. The driving license of the respondent no. 1 was also got verified which was found to be a learner's license. The IO recorded the statements of all the injured persons including the petitioner. Chargesheet was filed under section 279/337 IPC and section 3/181 and 5/180 MV Act for driving the vehicle without a valid license. Charge- sheet/challan was filed before the concerned court of Ld. MM and DAR was filed before this Tribunal. 5. Respondent no.1 (driver) as well as respondent no. 2 (owner) filed a common written statement on 27.02.2023 and respondent no. 3/insurance company filed its reply on 27.02.2023. Respondent nos.1 & 2 have stated in their written statement that they have been falsely implicated in the alleged accident and the petitioner has not come to the court with clean hands and suppressed material facts. Respondent no. 1 further stated that he has a valid driving license valid from 08.12.2021 to 07.06.2022 and he has always driven the vehicle with due care and diligence. 6. Respondent no. 3 has stated that respondent no.1 was driving the offending vehicle on the basis of a learner's license but he was not accompanied by any person holding a valid driving license and thus, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify respondent nos. 1 and 2. Phoolwati(I)(Fir 202/2022/Timar Pur) vs Aslam S/O. Aluddin on 5 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59284985/ 2 MACT No. 745/2022 Phoolwati Vs. Aslam & ors. Page 3 of 29 ISSUES FRAMED 7. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, vide order dated 27.02.2023, this Tribunal had framed the following issues: i. OPP iii. Relief. Evidence: 8. Local Commissioner was appointed for recording of evidence of the parties who filed the report on 16.01.2024. The petitioner Smt. Phoolwati was examined as PW-1 and Sh. Bhim Sain was examined as PW-2. The respondents examined Mr. Aslam as R1W2; Mr. Allauddin as R1W2 and Mr. Gulfam as R1W3. Respondent no. 3 did not lead any evidence. 9. The petitioner filed the Form XIV. Financial statement of the petitioner was recorded. 13. Bill No. 2329 issued 11.07.2022 700/- by Sharma Opticals (no relation to the accident) Total Rs. 9,963/- 27. The respondents have not disputed the above medical bills. Also, the MLC mentions that the petitioner/ injured had suffered injury on her upper lip and lower lip and also lost few teeth thus, this Tribunal is of the view that the petitioner/ injured must have incurred the above expense on her medical treatment. Therefore, an amount of Rs. 9,963/- is awarded to the petitioner/ injured Phoolwati towards medical expenses. Loss of income: 28. Coming to the aspect of loss of income, the petitioner Phoolwati claimed that she was working in a private job in an iron factory and was earning Rs. 20,000/- per month, but due to the accident in question she could not work for 6 months and suffered complete loss of earnings during that period. However, the petitioner has not filed any document to show that she was working in an iron factory or that she was earning Rs.20,000/- per month. Moreover, considering the injury of the Petitioner, it does not seem that the petitioner would have suffered any loss of income. Thus, she is not held entitled to any amount under this head. Mental shock: 29. The petitioner/ injured has claimed Rs. 50,000/- under this head, however, there is no cogent evidence on record regarding the same. However, taking into account the injuries suffered by her, Rs.5,000/- is awarded to the petitioner under the head of mental shock. Pain and Suffering: 30. The petitioner/ injured has claim Rs. 1,00,000/- under the head pain and suffering, however, no justification has been given for claiming such a huge amount. It is true that a particular amount cannot be fixed under the head pain and suffering which could be applicable to all cases as it varies Phoolwati(I)(Fir 202/2022/Timar Pur) vs Aslam S/O. Aluddin on 5 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59284985/ 10 from case to case. Judicial notice can be taken of the fact that since the petitioner has received certain injuries, therefore, petitioner must have suffered pain and sufferings owing to the said injuries. Considering the nature of injuries suffered by the injured/petitioner as mentioned in the MLC, this Tribunal hereby grants compensation of Rs. 5,000/- towards pain and sufferings to the petitioner. Special Diet: 31. The petitioner has claimed Rs. 50,000/- under the head special diet but there is no cogent evidence on record regarding money spent by the petitioner upon special diet. However, considering the nature of injuries suffered by the injured/petitioner, this Tribunal is of the opinion that petitioner must have spent some money under this head. Hence, this Tribunal hereby grant compensation of Rs. 5,000/- towards expenses incurred on special diet. Conveyance charges: 32. The petitioner has claimed Rs. 50,000/- under the head conveyance charges but there is no cogent evidence for the same. However, considering the nature of injuries suffered by the injured/petitioner, this Tribunal is of the opinion that petitioner must have incurred some expense on conveyance. Hence, this Tribunal hereby grant compensation of Rs. 5,000/- towards conveyance charges. Attendant charges: 33. The petitioner/ injured has claimed Rs. 50,000/- under this head, however, there is no cogent evidence on record for the money spent by the petitioner upon an attendant. Future treatment: 34. The petitioner has claimed expense towards future treatment, however, she has not filed any document to show that she could incur further expense on her treatment. Thus, she is held not entitled to any amount under this head. Any other loss/expenditure Nil. Mental & Physical Shock & Pain & Rs. 5,000/- + Rs. 5,000/-= Suffering Rs. 10,000/- Special diet Rs. 5,000/- Attendant charges Rs. 5,000/- Conveyance charges Rs. 5,000/- Loss of amenities Nil. Loss of earning, inconvenience, Nil. hardship, disappointment, frustration, mental stress, dejectment and unhappiness in future life etc. Total Rs. 34,963/- 36. Therefore, it is held that the petitioner shall be entitled to interest @ 6% per annum from the date of filing of DAR i.e. 12.09.2022 till realization. DISBURSEMENT 37. It is held that on realization of the award amount of Rs.34,963/-, the entire amount plus entire interest amount be released to the petitioner/claimant Phoolwati. 4 . Total Rs. 34,963/- 1(i+ii+iii+iv)+2(i+ii) 5. Total Compensation Rs. 34,963/- Interest awarded 6% 6. Earlier award amount (which has already been received by the petitioner in terms of previous award passed by Ld. - Predecessor) to be deducted from present award amount . 7. Ltd. 41. On the point of liability, Ld. Counsel for respondent no.3/ Insurance Company has submitted that respondent no. 1 was driving on a learner's license and there was no person with a valid driving license accompanying him at the time of the accident. He argued that thus, there was a violation of the terms of insurance policy and therefore, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify the respondents.
